title: 2021 AMC 12A Problem 19
statement: How many solutions does the equation \[ \sin\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\cos x\right) = \cos\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\sin x\right) \] have in the closed interval \([0, \pi]?\)

solutions.text:
Write the right side as \(\cos\left(\tfrac{\pi}{2}\sin x\right) = \sin\left(\tfrac{\pi}{2} - \tfrac{\pi}{2}\sin x\right).\) Equal sines require either \[ \begin{aligned} &\frac{\pi}{2}\cos x \\ &= \frac{\pi}{2}(1 - \sin x) + 2\pi k \end{aligned} \] or \[ \begin{aligned} &\frac{\pi}{2}\cos x \\ &= \pi - \frac{\pi}{2}(1 - \sin x) + 2\pi k. \end{aligned} \]

The first reduces to \(\cos x + \sin x = 1 + 4k;\) since \(\cos x + \sin x \in [-\sqrt2, \sqrt2],\) only \(k = 0\) works, giving \(\cos x + \sin x = 1,\) with solutions \(x = 0\) and \(x = \tfrac{\pi}{2}\) in \([0, \pi].\) The second reduces to \(\cos x - \sin x = 1,\) whose only solution in \([0, \pi]\) is \(x = 0.\)

The distinct solutions are \(x = 0\) and \(x = \tfrac{\pi}{2},\) for a total of \(2.\)

Thus, the correct answer is C.
hints: Equal sines give \(\cos x + \sin x = 1\) or \(\cos x - \sin x = 1;\) each has range \([-\sqrt2, \sqrt2]\)
